chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: Dr. Leo Mayer, the humanitarian who refused payment
summary: Cobb praises Dr. Mayer, Roosevelt's doctor, who would not take the $500 offered of the $1,500 owed, and remembers him courting after his wife died.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: He was a wonderful doctor, wasn't he?
He -- well, he was President Roosevelt's doctor.
How do you spell his name?
Mayer, M-a-y-e-r.
M-a-y-e-r, Dr. Leo B. Mayer. I don't know if he's living or dead today.
: He must have taken a real interest in you.

He did after he met me, but I had to go through somebody, and I owed him $1,500.00, and I went to him after he let me go back to work with a walking cast on. I BROUGHT $500. (Inaudible) when I talked to him, he said, 'I told you, when I get you back on your feet, then you start to paying me.' He wouldn't accept the $500.00. He was a humanitarian as well The fellow's a doctor.
And, you know, some doctors are greedy.
: Oh, sure.

He didn't want the money really. And $1,500.00 is all I owed him for all the time that he treated me and come to my house, and I went to his office afterwards. That's all that man -- and hospital costs. Don't you know doctors all that time will charge you more money? This man was beautiful.
: Well, that must have been a great consolation.
It was. His wife dropped dead on the streets of New York with a heart attack, and I'm still under him during this time, but I'm still in bed. I hadn't gotten

up then. And by the time I got up then to go to his office, he was courting. And I was supposed to go in one day, and I was late. And he was mad as hell at me. So he went to the barbershop and got a haircut --
(Side 10)
Well, just finish --
No, but --
Well, just finish (inaudible) what you were talking about connect up.
because otherwise it doesn't make (inaudible) what?
Talk about the (inaudible).
You know, what is it you think is courting--
What, Dr. Mayer was courting?
Yeah, just (inaudible) -- FINISH UP
He had him a gal -- you know, you need --

when I went to him, he was 76 years old. And but beautiful 76, was spry and could walk fast and do everything he want to do, well kept. And I admired the man so much because -- and then he was doing a lot for me, and I just loved the way he talked to me, because he told me that -- told my wife, he said, 'Dear, let the windows up. It's cold in the wintertime now. Put your sweater on and let him get some air in because we need to heal the -- need calcium and oxygen and all this to heal the bone up, you know. And you may get a little cool. Put a sweater on.' That's how cute -- he was just as cute as
he could be. And my wife did it, that gal right there.
